divergence: Default body is plain text, not Markdown (docx: oracle 112B vs rip 62B; csv r199 tab-joined vs 'a,b,c'). Accept: application/json returns {text,metadata} (oracle 406). Accept text/html: rip 200 (oracle 406). Empty body: rip 415 vs oracle 422 empty. Garbage: rip 415 vs oracle 200 empty. Corrupt docx: rip 422 vs oracle 200 partial text. 100000-char default cap gives rip 422 where oracle returns 200001B/3MB. POST accepted (oracle 405).

divergence: Returns a JSON array like upstream, but: keys are X-TIKA:* plus legacy names with always-array values (upstream tk:* scalar-or-array); content is plain text in X-TIKA:content (upstream Markdown tk:content); far fewer metadata keys (docx 941B vs 2199B, pdf 438B vs 1627B, zip 1144B vs 3557B); embedded path '/document/image1.png' vs '/image1.png'. Failures: upstream returns 200 with the exception recorded in metadata for empty/garbage/corrupt input (r097-r100) where rip returns 415/422 and loses all records. Output cap: rip 422 on 3MB text (r216), zip entries over the ratio limit 422 (r218,r219) where oracle returns 200. Content-Type hint ignored (r204).

divergence: Detected MIME is identical in r134-r143, r146, r151 and r226 (txt, docx, pdf, zip, png, html, empty, garbage, attachment filename hints); it differs only where rip honours a filename hint the oracle ignores (r144,r145). divergence: Contract differs: oracle returns bare ISO 639-1 text ('en','de'); rip returns JSON {language:'eng'|'deu'|'und', confidence, isReasonablyCertain} with ISO 639-3 codes. confidence observed 0.9 for en (r227,r228) and de (r155). Empty/short input: oracle empty/'ts', rip 'und'. Clients expecting 'en' break.

divergence: Body 'ripstream 0.0.0' vs 'Apache Tika 4.2.0'; clients that parse 'Apache Tika x.y.z' fail. /version/ trailing slash and HEAD /version 404 in rip (oracle 200). Accept: application/json 406 upstream, 200 in rip.

Same path, different schema: rip {status,active,queued,gate,isolation}; upstream {status:'OPERATING',active_tasks,millis_since_last_parse_started,files_processed}. Oracle 404 under its endpoint config, so the upstream response was not observed live (schema from source). rip's /status is not gated.
note: unverified live for upstream.

divergence: Oracle: html (341KB), text/plain (81KB), JSON (138KB) listings and per-type detail; 404 for unknown type.

divergence: 404 in rip. Oracle lists detector composition by org.apache.tika.* class name (html/json/text).

divergence: 404 in rip. Oracle lists parsers by Java class name with supported types (json 10KB/21KB).
note: Same reasoning as U26; the supported-types half overlaps U25.

divergence: Oracle 404 (opt-in), so upstream behaviour is source-only. Different contracts: upstream takes one FetchEmitTuple; rip takes a batch {source:{type,path|urls}, sink, concurrency, mode}. Verified on a second rip instance: JSON-only (415 otherwise), path traversal and absolute paths 403, http source 403 unless allowHttp, sink without sinkRoot refused, bad JSON 400. A single failing document aborts the whole run (i025 corrupt pdf in a 2-file dir -> 422 'Unable to read PDF', no per-document result; i014 a zip bomb in the dir -> 422) and the sink keeps files written before the failure (i018 left sink/out1/bundle.zip.txt). Per-document status is not returned although stats.failed exists in the success shape (i023).
note: Upstream maps per-document results to HTTP statuses (resource/PipesParsingHelper.java:469-507).

divergence: Oracle 404 (opt-in). Different contract: upstream takes a JSON list of FetchEmitTuples, queues them, returns {status:'ok',added:n} or 429 {status:'throttled'} + Retry-After when the queue stays full; there is no job id. rip takes a raw document body, returns 202 {id} and exposes GET /status/{id} polling (done/error/running). rip /async is always on (no gating) and returns 503 when too many jobs run.
note: Upstream's only 429 is here; spec/04's '429 for the concurrency limit' matches /async only.

upstream: Endpoint gating (endpoints set; pipes/async/status opt-in; allowPipes; allowPerRequestConfig -> 403)
ripstream: packages/server/src/index.ts:309-373 (route table fixed; only /pipes gated by options.pipes)
divergence: rip has no per-endpoint enable list: /status, /async, /health always on, /pipes off unless programmatic option. No 403 gating concept.
note: spec/04 2.1 says /async and /status share /pipes gating; the code does not.

divergence: Oracle 406 with empty body on any unsatisfiable Accept (8 requests rip answered 200, 2 answered 415/422). rip ignores Accept except 'application/json' on /tika and for error bodies. Accept: */*, */*;q=0.1 and q-lists fine (r231-r233).

Upstream error bodies are plain text, often empty (406/422) or a stack trace (r168 1213B, r047 96B). rip: plain text message by default, {error,code} JSON when Accept contains application/json. spec/04 2.2 claims a 4.x JSON body {status,message,exception}: neither implementation does that.
note: Spec drift, not a rip defect.

upstream: Parse-failure semantics (partial output vs hard error)
divergence: Upstream degrades: JSON endpoints return 200 with the exception stored in metadata plus whatever was extracted (corrupt docx rmeta 6847B, corrupt pdf 2692B, garbage 354B, empty 1518B); text endpoints return 422 with the partial body (r220) or 200 with partial text (r057); unknown binary is 200 with empty text. rip fails the whole request: 415 for no parser, 422 for malformed/encrypted/limit, with no partial records. Embedded-document failures lose the whole recursion.
note: Largest behavioural divergence for batch ingestion clients.

divergence: rip CLI default 100000 chars; exceeding gives a hard 422 'Output exceeds N characters', not truncation. Oracle returned 200001B and 3.2MB text with no limit, and ignores ?maxOutputChars and the writeLimit header (r073,r074,r208-r210). spec/04 7 calls 100000 'upstream-compatible' but the server has no such cap.
note: rip-only ?maxOutputChars with 400 on bad values (r209).

divergence: 413 in both. Default 100 MiB in rip vs 1 GiB upstream (spec/04 7 says 1 GiB). A declared Content-Length over the cap with a tiny body is not rejected early by either (both waited out the probe).
After a 413 on a 105 MiB body, the next request on the same keep-alive connection fails with ECONNRESET in rip (sequence 413,200,ECONNRESET,200,200); oracle 200 x5. Reproduced twice.
note: Cause (undrained request body) not verified.

divergence: 40 simultaneous /rmeta pdf: oracle 40x200; rip 21x200 + 19x503 (Retry-After 1) under the CLI's memory-derived gate. /detect burst: both 40x200. Upstream /tika never returns 429/503 under this load; its only 429 is the /async queue. spec/04 says 429.
note: Defensible design difference; document it.

divergence: rip: single requestTimeoutMs (60 s) covering parse and queue wait (408), plus Node's requestTimeout. Upstream: separate read deadline 408, response write deadline, idle timeout. Not exercised.
note: unverified.

divergence: BUG: extractMultipart decodes the body with TextDecoder('latin1'), which WHATWG maps to windows-1252, then re-encodes with Buffer.from(...,'latin1'). 27 byte values (0x80,0x82-0x8c,0x8e,0x91-0x9c,0x9e,0x9f) do not round-trip, so any binary part with those bytes is corrupted (docx via multipart -> 422 'Unable to inflate word/document.xml', r173; plain text works r060). Also: multipart is detected by Content-Type on any PUT/POST route; a multipart body PUT to /tika returns 422 where the oracle 200 empty (r198); only the first part carrying filename= is used (static; part without filename unverified).
note: Fix is a one-liner: decode with Buffer.latin1/binary or parse bytes.

divergence: Oracle: attachment Content-Disposition filename (r142,r143,r200), Content-Type hint (r204 text/csv). Not honoured by oracle: inline disposition, File-Name header, ?filename= (r144,r145,r201-r203). rip: honours ?filename= and any Content-Disposition filename; ignores Content-Type hint (r204) and File-Name header (r202). Net: Content-Type hint missing in rip.

upstream: HTTP gzip: request Content-Encoding, response Accept-Encoding
divergence: Oracle gzips responses when asked (Content-Encoding: gzip, Vary: Accept-Encoding) and inflates gzip request bodies. rip never sets Content-Encoding. A gzip request body parses in rip (r194,r195 equal text) only because the parser unwraps the gzip format, not because of Content-Encoding handling. Response compression not observable on rip (r197 hit the output cap) - static only.
Both 200 with identical 81B text.

upstream: Method matrix: HEAD, OPTIONS, POST on PUT-only routes
divergence: HEAD: oracle 200, rip 404/405. OPTIONS: oracle 200 + Allow header, rip 204 with no Allow. POST on /tika,/rmeta,/meta,/detect,/unpack: oracle 405/415, rip 200 (more permissive). PUT/GET/DELETE/PATCH 405 behaviours align (r013,r014,r112,r149,r159,r177).

upstream: Path matching: trailing slash, dot segments, case
divergence: Oracle accepts trailing slash on /version, /tika/, /rmeta/ (200); rip 404. /tika/../version: oracle 404 (no normalisation), rip 200 (WHATWG URL normalises). //tika/text: oracle 400, rip 404. Uppercase path 404 in both.

rip survived all probes. Differences: invalid %zz in path: oracle 400 html vs rip 404; invalid %zz in query: oracle 500 stacktrace vs rip 200; 20KB URI: oracle 414 vs rip 431; absolute-form, HTTP/1.0, no Host, garbage line, Expect: 100-continue: equivalent. Declared Content-Length of 2 GiB/1 GiB+1/200 MiB with 3 bytes sent: both stall (no early reject).

Both off by default (no Access-Control-* on any oracle or CLI-rip response). rip with corsOrigin list (verified, second instance): preflight 204 echoes a listed origin, omits it for an unlisted origin, Vary: Origin, Allow-Headers fixed to 'Content-Type, Accept'. Upstream: one origin or '*' via CXF filter; behaviour with cors on not observed.
note: unverified for upstream with cors enabled; CLI has no flag.
